Edit: But seriously, that would be very time consuming. That's the only reason I can think of right now. If anyone can point out the other downsides don't hesitate to respond.

Policies need to be debated, not just voted on. While a parliament can narrow down the most popular standpoint relatively fast, a whole country full of people may take a while to make a draft.
The time consumption can also be further elaborated: In a case of war reactions need to be fast and efficient, setting up an election and double checking the votes will cost lives.
Also, as time is money, every election costs the taxpayer a lot (about 1$/vote, can scale up extremely depending on the complexity of the ballot and anti-fraud measures taken). I think most people would gladly pay that for an election on TTIP and while politicians cost a lot of money too, they also vote on policies with almost no controversies. Without politicians there is no "filter" for these smaller policies, which will fill up your free time and mailbox pretty fast.
All of these are technical implementation details if the system were an online one.

I agree with you, an online voting system would eliminate most of these problems, but it also raises many other concerns. Your online vote is not anonymous (and therefore susceptible to threats) as the site will track your IP. Using a proxy is not an option: No one should trust a foreigner who can manipulate votes - especially if there is a great incentive to do exactly that. This also leads to the conclusion, that no one should trust the software run on a server with their votes.
Worst of all, many PCs are already infected with malware. If the voting site is not rigged or hacked, there is always the possibilty that a hacker, who does not even need to be from your country and therefore can not even be hold accountable by your jurisdiction, influences the complete election with a computerworm. The greater the incentive, the more creative humans get. To fake a million paper votes, at least a million actions are required and the fraud becomes obvious. There is no huge difference in faking ten electronic votes or a millon.

 

Tl;dr: Electronic voting can never replace paper voting in a democracy.
